note: STATUS, MEASURED 2026-08-23: this manifest is authored and the engine CANNOT RUN AGAINST IT.
`mock-affordances.py` slices a section and then slices a `.v-<state>` frame inside it, and
`#statusPopover` has no such frame — it is one unframed surface, where `#b-servers` and `#swin`
carry `.v-ideal` / `.v-empty` blocks. The gate therefore exits 3 with
`error: #statusPopover has no '.v-ideal' block`, which is the designed could-not-run exit and
not a clean surface. Recorded as a difference rather than a pass, and the fix is either a
whole-section fallback in that script for a surface declaring one state, or state frames in the
mock. Neither is M20's: the first is a shared gate whose blast radius is every surface, and the
second edits the design of record to satisfy an instrument.
What DID get measured, and what M20's acceptance actually rests on, is the structure dump this
surface now produces. `MeasureDump --surface popover --state ideal` writes 12 nodes, and
`planning/evidence/M20-acceptance.md` reads criterion 4 off it: three separately focusable
controls in the queued-item band, at three disjoint frames on one horizontal axis. That is the
only lane that reaches this surface at all — `SURF-009` carries three `n/a` cases whose stated
reason is that NSStatusItem is not an AXPress target while the app is backgrounded, so the
popover cannot be opened or photographed by the accessibility campaign.
ONE AFFORDANCE-DERIVATION FACT worth knowing before anyone trusts a future ledger for this
surface: the mock's four header count cells are plain `div`s carrying `small muted` and `mono`,
which match NONE of `mock-affordances.py`'s rules, so the derived inventory has 14 rows and none
of them is a count. `Resident 214 MB` — the one number in this popover that does not ship — would
therefore never appear as an absent affordance however long the gate ran. It is declared in the
pairing file's header and enforced structurally instead, by `MenuBarPresentation.Counts` having no
field it could come from (`MenuBarPresentationTests.headerHasNoSkillsField`).
INSTRUMENTATION COVERAGE IS PARTIAL AND THAT IS NOT THE SAME AS THE BUILD BEING PARTIAL. The
`.measured` calls on this surface cover the header counts and the decision band — the zone
criterion 4 is about. The call log, the stale notice, the attention band and the footer are drawn
by the build and are NOT instrumented, so they pair to `-` in the pairing file with that reason
cited. A reader must not read those rows as the build lacking a call log.
The floors below are the census sizes measured on the run that wrote them and are a ratchet:
a layer reading fewer rows than its floor exits 3, not 0, because a shrunken denominator raises
